item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q022_colg_crya_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.04 the ColG collagen-binding domain from PDB 1nqd and the Cry3A C-terminal domain from PDB 1dlc were only in the same all-beta class, not in the same fold or superfamily. 1nqd chain A, d1nqda_, and the other 1nqd copy, then d1nqdb_, were classified as b.23.2.1: class b All beta proteins, fold b.23 CUB-like, superfamily b.23.2 Collagen-binding domain, family b.23.2.1 Collagen-binding domain. The Cry3A C-terminal domain d1dlca1, residues 500-644, was already b.18.1.3: class b, fold b.18 Galactose-binding domain-like, superfamily b.18.1 Galactose-binding domain-like, family b.18.1.3 delta-Endotoxin, C-terminal domain. In the current public SCOPe release, 2.08, 1nqd d1nqda_ and the corresponding chain-B structural core d1nqdb1, residues 893-1008, have been moved into b.18.1 as family b.18.1.36 Collagen-binding domain. Thus the ColG domain and 1dlc d1dlca1 now share a SCOPe superfamily, b.18.1, which is the level that asserts common ancestry; they are still deliberately kept in different families, b.18.1.36 versus b.18.1.3, so the classification supports remote homology of the beta-sandwich domain scaffold, not direct transfer of collagen binding, delta-endotoxin specificity, organism, or detailed receptor preference between the proteins. Structurally, this is a jelly-roll beta-sandwich relationship: the old CUB-like b.23 fold was annotated as a 10-strand, 2-sheet jelly-roll sandwich, and the current shared b.18 fold is annotated as a 9-strand, 2-sheet jelly-roll sandwich. Functionally and phylogenetically, SCOPe records external literature support on the new Collagen-binding domain family: PubMed 17977833 is annotated as describing likely homology among d1nqdb_ from ColG, d1w99a3 from a Bacillus thuringiensis Cry toxin C-terminal domain in the same b.18.1.3 family as Cry3A d1dlca1, and d2quoa_ from the related Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin C-terminal family b.18.1.37. That evidence makes the 2.08 placement a remote-homology merge within b.18.1; the fold b.18 level by itself would not imply homology, and individual PDB domains such as 1nqd or 1dlc should be treated as release-specific domain examples rather than as a license to choose a template or transfer function across every b.18 fold member.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1nqd/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1dlc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1nqd/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dlc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1nqda_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1dlca1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1nqda_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dlca1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1w99a3/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d2quoa_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.04/sunids/49853/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49784/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49784/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49785/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267607/annotations"]}]}
